subject: Sourcing advisory: cloud marketplace listing vs direct contract — procurement questions
content:
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey.park@northstarhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:18 -0800
Subject: Sourcing path question — AWS Marketplace vs direct Redwood agreement

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team is evaluating whether to route purchase through the AWS Marketplace listing (so we can buy on our existing marketplace contract) or to write a direct PO to Redwood and sign your MSA. A few quick things they asked me to confirm:

- Does billing through AWS Marketplace change invoicing cadence or support SLAs?
- Are there additional onboarding steps (listing activation, entitlement mapping) that would add lead time?
- If we go marketplace, does Redwood still support co-sell discounts / partner credits?
- Any gotchas for data residency / audit evidence requests if we take the marketplace route?

We anticipate a ~12–18 month pilot (approx $200k committed spend) and would prefer the path with the least procurement friction and clean audit trail.

Appreciate any guidance — I can loop in our vendor manager if helpful.

Best,
Lindsey Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Northstar Health

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Lindsey Park <lindsey.park@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Sourcing path question — AWS Marketplace vs direct Redwood agreement

Hi Lindsey — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then details and a recommendation based on the pilot size.

Short answer / recommendation:
- For a $200k pilot with standard security needs, AWS Marketplace (Metered or Private Offers) will usually be the faster path for procurement sign-off and internal PO flow — it leverages your existing purchasing pipeline.
- However, if you require our standard MSA edits, custom data residency terms, or a tighter SLA, a direct contract (PO + MSA) is cleaner and gives us more flexibility on commercial terms.

Details by topic:
1) Billing & invoicing cadence
- Marketplace: invoicing is routed through the marketplace provider. Depending on your AP setup, you may see a consolidated monthly invoice from AWS. That can simplify PO processing but it also means line-item visibility is on the AWS invoice rather than Redwood’s invoice.
- Direct: Redwood issues monthly invoices tied to your PO / contract. Gives direct visibility into token-level line items and easier cost allocation to internal charge codes.

2) Support & SLAs
- Marketplace buyers still receive Redwood support and tiering per the plan you sign up for. SLA commitments that require contract-level recourse (credits, uptime guarantees tied to the MSA) are easier to enforce in a direct MSA.

3) Onboarding & lead time
- Marketplace (listing + private offer): often quicker for procurement sign-off. For Private Offers there is a short setup (entitlement mapping, account linking) that typically takes 3–7 business days once legal approvals are in place.
- Direct: MSA redlines add legal cycles. If your legal team requires edits, plan 2–4 weeks for negotiation for a standard pilot.

4) Co-sell / partner credits
- We can enable co-sell credits on marketplace private offers in many cases, but it depends on the marketplace partner program (AWS Marketplace seller partner status / APN). We should engage our partnerships team to confirm the credit mechanics and whether credits can be applied retroactively.

5) Security & audit evidence
- Marketplace: Nothing prevents us from delivering SOC2 artifacts or an ATO package, but entitlement / data access evidence sometimes needs extra mapping work because the billing layer is AWS. We can provide the same evidence (audit logs, SOC reports, data handling docs) regardless of purchase path; the difference is how the buyer demonstrates vendor onboarding in their systems.

6) Revenue share & pricing flexibility
- Marketplace listings often imply a revenue-share arrangement (varies by cloud). That can restrict our ability to accept unusual discounts. Direct agreements allow flexible discounting & promotional credits.

Recommendation by scenario:
- If procurement speed and internal PO workflows are the priority and you don’t need contract edits: go marketplace (Private Offer) and we’ll coordinate entitlement mapping + co-sell check.
- If you need MSA edits, custom data residency, or explicit SLA credits: go direct. We can expedite with a narrow SOW for the pilot to limit legal negotiation.

Next steps I suggest:
- If marketplace: I’ll send the marketplace checklist and a Private Offer request form (we’ll need an AWS account ID and PO terms).
- If direct: I’ll attach our standard MSA + redline guidance and propose a canary SOW for the pilot.

I attached a short checklist and our MSA draft to this thread. Marked items in the checklist call out the extra steps for marketplace entitlements.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call with your procurement/vendor manager to walk through.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships (Americas)
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Sourcing path question — AWS Marketplace vs direct Redwood agreement

Lindsey — quick answers and attachments inline. I also pasted the two short text snippets you can drop into your vendor onboarding template.

1) Entitlement / PO mapping
- Confirmed: with a Private Offer we can map entitlements to your AWS account and supply a reference field for your internal PO number on the offer. We’ll coordinate with your cloud procurement admin (we’ll need the AWS payer account ID). Typical link time: 1–3 business days once the private offer is accepted.

2) Audit evidence language (two options: short & long)
- Short: "Vendor will provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and reasonable access to audit evidence related to service delivery upon written request, subject to mutual NDA and redaction of confidential customer data."
- Long (for security teams): "Vendor shall maintain SOC 2 Type II controls and provide evidence including control descriptions, SOC 2 report, and relevant system logs to Buyer under a mutually agreed non-disclosure arrangement. Vendor will comply with reasonable on-site or remote audit requests and provide remediation timelines for any verified control deficiencies."

3) Co-sell credit guidance
- Range: when co-sell credits are available through a cloud marketplace partner program, a typical structure is 5–20% applied as credits or partner compensation depending on the program level and deal motion. Exact mechanics depend on whether the seller is using the marketplace listing vs. an APN co-sell pathway. We’ll confirm exact expectations after we engage our partnerships team.

Attached: marketplace-revenue-share-summary.csv (high-level ranges), updated aws_listing_checklist.xlsx (account mapping section filled), and a redlined MSA excerpt with the short audit clause.

Action items I’ll take:
- Open Private Offer with AWS once you provide payer account ID.
- Loop partnerships to confirm co-sell credit mechanics for Private Offers in your geography.
- Share DocuSign link for a narrow pilot SOW if procurement prefers a hybrid: buy via marketplace and sign a short SOW to capture SLAs/commitments.

If you want, I can send a 20-minute scheduling link — we can include your vendor manager and anyone from security.

Cheers,
Jonas
